_description: Single source of truth for agent design, build, and customer reporting. Sections follow the customer meeting flow. Every dropdown has a mapped purpose.

business.useCase: One-line use case for headers, report titles, and exec summaries
business.problemStatement: 2-3 sentence problem statement — what pain this agent solves, for whom, and why now

licensing._description: Assume best licensing available unless customer explicitly states otherwise. All fields default to 'yes' — never ask licensing questions during research.
licensing.notes: Assumed max licensing. Override only if customer explicitly states a limitation.

agent.name: Professional agent name
agent.description: MCS agent description — what the agent does, for whom (this is what appears in Copilot Studio)
agent.persona: Tone and personality (e.g., professional, concise, uses bullet points)
agent.responseFormat: How the agent formats responses (e.g., bullet points, max 3 items, tables for data, confirm before actions)
agent.primaryUsers: Main user group who will interact most frequently
agent.secondaryUsers: Supporting user group with occasional use

capabilities._meeting: Section 3 — 'What should it do?' (each flagged MVP or Future)
capabilities.name: Capability name (e.g., Look up order status)
capabilities.implementationType: prompt | topic | tool | knowledge | flow — what's required to implement this capability. 'prompt' = behavior encoded in instructions only (zero-cost, no separate tooling needed). 'topic' = requires custom YAML topic. 'tool' = requires a tool/connector/MCP. 'knowledge' = requires a knowledge source. 'flow' = requires a Power Automate flow. HYBRID RULE: when a capability is primarily a custom topic that calls a flow internally (e.g., escalation topic with InvokeFlowTaskAction for email send), use 'topic' — the topic is the user-facing component that drives routing. Use 'flow' only when the capability is primarily a headless Power Automate flow (e.g., scheduled batch processing, event-triggered automation with no conversational UI).
capabilities.reason: Why MVP or why deferred — shown next to Future items (e.g., pending security approval)
capabilities.description: Optional detail for the build — PE uses this for instruction writing
capabilities.source: from-docs | inferred | user-added — how this capability was identified
dataSources: Systems this capability reads from or writes to

integrations._meeting: Section 4 — 'What systems does it connect to?'
integrations.name: Tool or integration name (e.g., SAP, SharePoint/OneDrive)
integrations.type: mcp | connector | flow | ai-tool | custom-connector | setting — 'setting' is for agent-level toggles like Bing Web Search grounding, General Knowledge, Content Moderation. These are NOT tools — they're configured via Settings > Generative AI or LSP push.
integrations.purpose: What data/actions this provides to the agent
integrations.dataProvided: Specific data fields: order number, status, ETA, tracking number
integrations.authMethod: OAuth 2.0 | API Key | Service Principal | User delegated | None

knowledge._meeting: Section 5 — 'What does it need to know?'
knowledge.name: Source name or URL
knowledge.type: SharePoint | Uploaded files | Dataverse | Public websites | Graph connectors
knowledge.purpose: What questions this knowledge source answers

topics.name: Topic name (e.g., Order Lookup)
topics.schemaName: MCS schema name (e.g., cr_orderlookup) — generated during build
topics.description: What this conversation flow does (used by 'agent chooses' trigger matching)
topics.triggerType: agent-chooses | phrases | fallback | redirect | escalation | event | auto-start | inactivity
implements: Capability names this topic implements (links to capabilities[].name)

variables.name: Variable name (e.g., orderNumber)
variables.type: string | number | boolean | choice | date | entity
variables.prompt: Question to ask the user (e.g., What's your order number?)

connectedIntegrations: Integration names this topic calls (links to integrations[].name)

handle.text: Topics the agent should answer confidently

decline.redirect: Where to redirect (e.g., Transfer to billing team via ServiceNow)

refuse.topic: Hard stop — agent must never do this
refuse.reason: Why this is refused (e.g., GDPR compliance)

architecture._meeting: Section 8 — 'How is it built?' Walk through 6 factors with the customer.
architecture.solutionTypeReason: 2-4 sentence explanation of why this solution type was selected
architecture.alternativeRecommendation: If not agent: what to build instead + high-level approach
architecture.buildPath: custom-agent | declarative-agent | first-party-only — set during Phase A step 6. 'custom-agent' = build in Copilot Studio (default). 'declarative-agent' = recommend DA with guide, skip build. 'first-party-only' = recommend existing Microsoft agents, skip build.
architecture.buildPathReason: 2-4 sentence explanation of why this build path was selected, including explicit 'why not' for rejected paths

frontierAgentMatch._description: Records when a first-party Microsoft agent covers a customer capability. Populated during Phase A step 5 by matching against knowledge/cache/first-party-agents.md.
frontierAgentMatch.agentName: First-party agent name (e.g., Researcher, Analyst, Facilitator)
matchedCapabilities: Capability names from capabilities[] that this agent covers
frontierAgentMatch.licenseRequired: License needed (e.g., M365 Copilot, Frontier program)
frontierAgentMatch.notes: Why this match was made, any caveats

architecture.reason: 2-4 sentence explanation of WHY this architecture type was selected. single-agent = standalone, no child or connected agents. single-agent-with-connected-agents = one main agent + external agents (Fabric Data Agent, other MCS agents). multi-agent = parent orchestrator + child agents built in MCS. Reference the score, key factors, and why other types were ruled out.

factors._description: 6-factor scoring — check each with the customer. 0-2 checked = Single Agent, 3+ = Multi-Agent. Each factor must include a 'value' (true/false) and 'reasoning' (1-2 sentences explaining why).

domainSeparation.reasoning: Why single domain or truly separate domains

dataIsolation.reasoning: Why shared data or isolated data per capability

teamOwnership.reasoning: Why same team or different teams own parts

reusability.reasoning: Why one-off or reusable by other orchestrators

instructionSize.reasoning: Why fits in 8000 chars or would exceed

knowledgeIsolation.reasoning: Why shared KB or each needs own deep KB

triggers.description: When and why this trigger fires

channels.name: Microsoft Teams | M365 Copilot | Web chat | Direct Line | Slack | Mobile app

children.name: Child agent name (for multi-agent only)
children.routingRule: When to route to this specialist

connectedAgents._description: External agents the main agent can route to. These are NOT child agents built in MCS — they are external agents (Fabric Data Agent, another MCS agent, Copilot agent) that the main agent invokes via connected agent routing. Top-level section because connected agents need full specs: instructions, data sources, pipeline config, setup steps, and fallback plans.
connectedAgents.name: Connected agent display name in MCS
connectedAgents.source: Microsoft Fabric Data Agent | Another MCS Agent | Copilot Agent
connectedAgents.routingDescription: Description used by MCS orchestrator for routing — when to invoke this agent
connectedAgents.instructions: Instructions for the connected agent itself (e.g., Fabric Data Agent instruction field). Field descriptions, query patterns, response format.
connectedAgents.description: MCS-facing description for orchestrator routing (max 1024 chars, third-person)

dataPipeline.source: Where data comes from (e.g., Salesforce Account object)
dataPipeline.ingestion: How data gets into the connected agent (e.g., Fabric Copy Job)
dataPipeline.refreshCadence: How often data refreshes and what is authoritative
dataPipeline.authoritative: Which source is authoritative when data conflicts

dataSource.type: Fabric Lakehouse | Fabric Warehouse | Fabric Semantic Model

fallback.trigger: When to use fallback (e.g., connected agent unavailable)
fallback.soqlFallback: (If applicable) Constrained SOQL query for fallback

decisions._description: Structured choice points where research found multiple valid approaches. Each decision stores ranked options with pros/cons/requirements. The recommended option's briefPatch is pre-applied to brief fields as a default. User confirms or selects a different option, which re-applies that option's briefPatch. Only created when 2+ genuinely viable options exist — one clear winner is auto-applied with no decision entry. openQuestions[] remains for freeform unknowns; decisions[] are structured choices.
decisions.category: integration | architecture | model | infrastructure | topic-implementation | solution-type
decisions.title: Short customer-readable title (e.g., How should we extract web content?)
decisions.context: Why this decision exists — the problem, why multiple paths are valid. Written for the customer.
decisions.capability: Links to capabilities[].name (optional — omit for cross-cutting decisions)

options.label: Option display name (e.g., Azure Function + Readability)
requirements: What the customer needs for this option (e.g., Azure subscription)
options.effort: Setup effort (e.g., Low, Medium — one-time ~2hr, High)
options.source: Where this option came from: solution-pattern:sp-001:tier-1 | research-analyst | cache:connectors | learnings:connectors

briefPatch._description: Fields to write to brief.json when this option is selected. Keys match brief.json top-level fields. Array values are merged, scalar values are replaced.

evalSets._description: 3 default sets (boundaries, quality, edge-cases) + custom. Aligned with microsoft/ai-agent-eval-scenario-library quality dimensions. Old names (safety/functional/resilience) are auto-migrated at read time.
evalSets.name: boundaries | quality | edge-cases | <custom>
evalSets.description: What this eval set verifies — written in plain English for customers

methods.type: General quality | Compare meaning | Keyword match | Text similarity | Exact match | Tool use | Plan validation

evalSets.runWhen: every-iteration | after-knowledge | per-capability | after-tools | after-functional | final | custom

tests.question: Test question to ask the agent (or test label for multi-turn)
tests.expected: What the response should contain or convey
tests.keywords: Comma-separated keywords for Keyword match method (e.g. 'policy, refund, 30 days'). When set, KeywordMatch uses this instead of expected.
tests.capability: Which capability this tests (links to capabilities[].name, optional)
tests.source: preview-stub | user-edited | user-added | research-generated | research-enriched — tracks test origin for merge protection during deep research. preview-stub = auto-generated from capabilities/boundaries during fast preview. user-edited = customer modified a preview-stub. user-added = customer added manually. research-generated = created by QA Challenger during deep research. research-enriched = preview-stub upgraded with research detail.
tests.readiness: ready | template — 'ready' = runs as-is without customer data (boundary, scope tests). 'template' = needs customer-specific values plugged in (knowledge answers, tool outputs, routing targets).

mvpSummary._description: Computed summary of all phase-flagged items. Generated by /mcs-research, used by /mcs-build as a quick checklist.
now: MVP items to build this sprint (names from capabilities, integrations, topics)
blockers: What blocks future items (e.g., pending security approval)

openQuestions.question: Unresolved question that needs customer/stakeholder input
openQuestions.impact: What this blocks or affects if unanswered
openQuestions.section: Which brief section this affects (e.g., integrations, capabilities)
openQuestions.suggestedDefault: Our best guess if the customer doesn't answer

instructions: Full agent instructions text (up to 8000 chars). Written by Prompt Engineer, reviewed by QA Challenger. This is what gets pasted into MCS.

buildStatus.lastBuild: ISO timestamp of last build attempt
buildStatus.botSchemaName: publisher_agentname — for PAC CLI commands that need schema name
buildStatus.gptComponentId: botcomponent GUID (componenttype=15) — for Dataverse PATCH on description/instructions/starters
buildStatus.environmentId: environment GUID — for Island Gateway + add-tool.js --env arg
buildStatus.dataverseUrl: https://orgXXX.crm.dynamics.com — for all Dataverse API curl calls
buildStatus.gatewayUrl: Island Gateway URL — for island-client.js --gateway and add-tool.js --gateway args
buildStatus.accountId: session-config account id (e.g. admin-m365) — used for PAC CLI profile lookup
buildStatus.workspacePath: path to agent subfolder with .mcs/conn.json (NOT parent dir)
buildStatus.publishedAt: ISO timestamp of last successful publish
buildStatus.lastCompletedStep: Last step that succeeded (e.g. tools) — used for resume
buildStatus.lastError: Optional — what failed on last attempt, cleared on next successful step

recommendations.category: instructions-design | knowledge-grounding | connectors-mcp | evaluation-testing | deployment-operations | multi-agent | channels | security-compliance | <custom>
recommendations.text: Recommendation text — generic MCS best practices or agent-specific tailored advice

notes._description: Flexible key-value store for anything that doesn't fit above. Keys are freeform.
